result.note: Also in the news item; tested the non-fossil capacity share, the solar-wind split and the 2030 target in one statements question.

questions.prompt: In August 2026, India's installed non-fossil fuel electricity generation capacity crossed 300 GW. Consider the following statements:
items: Non-fossil sources make up over 54% of India's total installed power capacity of about 552 GW.
Wind power accounts for a larger share of this non-fossil capacity than solar power.
India's target is to reach 500 GW of non-fossil energy capacity by 2030.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong because solar leads with 164.59 GW against 58.14 GW for wind. The 300 GW mark puts India at over 60% of its 500 GW target for 2030, and domestically made solar cells became mandatory across all projects from June 2026.
questions.source: Non-fossil fuel sources now comprise over 54% of India’s total power capacity (~552 GW), led primarily by solar power (164.59 GW) and wind power (58.14 GW).
